session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance and one hidden link, held level across the band.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A large amount of water is stored in the ground, and it is still moving, though very slowly. Most of it comes from rain and snow that soaks down from the land surface. The upper layer of soil is the unsaturated zone, where water is present in varying amounts but does not fill the soil. Below that layer is the saturated zone, where water fills every pore, crack, and space between rock particles. That water is groundwater, and it may stay in storage for a long time before it moves on. Water moves down through the soil over time. It keeps moving.
passage.part_2: An aquifer is a layer of rock, sand, or soil underground that holds water and lets it move. People pump it for drinking and for farming. Aquifers are refilled by rain and snow that seeps down through the soil. How fast they refill depends on the rock, because some rocks pass water quickly while others hold it back. That is why some aquifers refill within a few years and others take a very long time. Water may also travel a long way underground before anyone pumps it. Farms and cities both rely on it. People use this water every day.

items.prompt: What is the difference between the unsaturated zone and the saturated zone?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The saturated zone has every space full of water.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage states that the unsaturated zone is not full and the saturated zone is full.
tutor_only.tell: In the unsaturated zone water passes through but the soil is not full. In the saturated zone every space is full.
help: Find the two sentences that name each zone.
One zone is full. The other is not.
tutor_only.core_idea: The saturated zone is full of water and the unsaturated zone is not.
accept_ideas: the saturated zone is full of water
one is full and one is not
the saturated zone has water in every space

if_they_say.when: the student says the unsaturated zone holds more water
if_they_say.ask: Check the word. Unsaturated means what about the spaces?

items.prompt: Why do some aquifers refill quickly and others very slowly?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. It depends on how fast water moves through the rock.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says refill speed depends on the rock, and that some rocks pass water while others hold it back.
tutor_only.tell: Rock that passes water lets an aquifer refill fast. Rock that holds water back slows the refill.
help: Look at the sentences about how fast aquifers refill.
They compare two kinds of rock.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because some rocks let water through quickly and others hold it back.
accept_ideas: some rocks let water pass quickly
rock that holds water back refills slowly
not_required: the name of a rock type

if_they_say.when: the student says aquifers refill at the same speed everywhere
if_they_say.ask: The passage says the speed depends on something. What is it?

items.prompt: The passage says groundwater is still moving, though very slowly. Why does that matter for a well?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Slow movement means water takes a long time to reach the well again.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage joins slow movement with slow refill of aquifers.
tutor_only.tell: Water moves slowly underground. A pumped well may wait a long time for water to come back.
help: Connect the slow movement sentence to the refill sentences.
Look at what slow water means for a person waiting on a well.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because the water a well removes comes back slowly, so refill takes time.

if_they_say.when: the student says groundwater never moves
if_they_say.ask: The passage says it moves. What word does it use to describe the speed?

items.prompt: Where does most of the water in the ground come from?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. Rain or snow that soaked down through the soil.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage states that most groundwater started as rain or snow that soaked down.
tutor_only.tell: Most groundwater began as rain or snow and soaked down through the soil.
help: Look at the sentence that says where most groundwater comes from.
It names two kinds of weather.
tutor_only.core_idea: From rain or snow that soaked into the soil.
accept_ideas: rain that seeped into the ground
not_required: how long the water takes to soak down

if_they_say.when: the student says the water comes from rivers
if_they_say.ask: The passage says rivers are not the source. What weather does it name?

items.prompt: Why do people need to know how fast an aquifer refills?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. Pumping faster than the refill uses up the stored water.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage links refill speed to how long the stored water lasts.
tutor_only.tell: Refill speed decides how much water can be pumped without using up the store.
help: Think about a store of water that refills slowly.
Look at what happens if people pump faster than the refill.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because pumping faster than the refill uses up the water.
accept_ideas: pumping faster than refill uses up the water
they need to know how much they can pump

if_they_say.when: the student says refill speed does not matter
if_they_say.ask: The passage says refill speed varies. Why would that matter to a farmer?
